answer.line: A positive standard potential means K is above 1. log K = 2 x 0.50 / 0.0592, about 17, so K is about 10^17.

steps: Read the sign first. A positive standard potential means the reaction runs forward on its own, so K is above 1.
Size it: log K = nE / 0.0592. With n = 2, every 0.0296 V is one power of ten.
Count the powers: 0.50 / 0.0296 is about 17. So K is about 10^17, far toward products.

choices.note: Using 0.1 for 0.0592 gives log K = 1.0 / 0.1 = 10. That rounding costs seven powers of ten.
K = 10 would need a potential of only about 0.03 V. Half a volt with two electrons is many powers of ten more.
No single slip gives 10^5; dropping n gives about 10^8.5. Count 0.0296 V per power of ten instead.
Right size, other side of 1. A positive standard potential favors products, so K sits far above 1.

lockIt: Positive standard potential means K above 1; log K = nE / 0.0592.

playWith.label: Nernst module: set the standard potential to 0.50 V and n to 2, slide log Q to 6, and see E stay well above 0

visual.bottomLabel: n = 2: each 0.0296 V is one power of ten in K

visual.alt: Two aligned rulers: standard potential in volts on top and K as powers of ten below, with 0 V lined up with K = 1. The given 0.50 V drops straight down to K = 10 to the 17, outlined. The other choices sit at 10 to the -17, 10, 10 to the 5 and 10 to the 10.
visual.caption: Start at 0.50 V on the top ruler and drop straight down. Positive volts land far out on the K above 1 side.
